title: Mirabel and the Oath
premise: Mirabel Quill, runaway apprentice turned ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers her own name and tonight's date in a century-old book of prophecies. The prophecy binds her to steal back the soul of a drowned child sold to the court beneath the mountain — a soul the Guild itself brokered, and one Dominic Delacroix, the charming guildsman she loves, was paid to protect. Torn between loyalty to the found family that took her in and the truth of what they've done, Mirabel descends into the under-court, bargains with its hungry queen, and learns the prophecy's final line names her own soul as the price. In the end she outwits the bargain by paying with something no court can hold — her memory of Dominic — returning home whole but hollowed, until he chooses to trade his guild standing to win that memory back.
about_author: Lior Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing estate sales full of unlabeled ledgers and half-burned letters. They write fantasy about people who keep records of things that were never supposed to be written down.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Tonight
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. While balancing the Guild's accounts in the flooded cellar-office, she finds a prophecy book dated 1897 open to today's page — bearing her name. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the ordinary world of ink and inventory cracks open, and she realizes someone in the Guild has known about this for a long time.

chapters.title: What the Guild Sold
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Following ledger entries backward, she uncovers the sale: a child's soul traded to the court beneath the mountain, brokered by the Guild, witnessed by Dominic's signature. She confronts him; he neither denies it nor explains. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpened by the fact that she still trusts him more than anyone alive.

chapters.title: The Drowned Child
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins with Odile, the mother whose daughter's soul was sold to buy the family's survival through a plague winter. Mirabel visits their river-house and sees what a soulless child looks like: breathing, obedient, empty-eyed. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve — this is no longer abstract accounting.

chapters.title: Terms of Apprenticeship
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV flashback interwoven with present. We learn how he came to the Guild as an orphan, how the Guildmaster became father, judge, and jailer to him, and why he signed as witness. Emotional beat: sympathy complicates anger — the reader sees Dominic was also sold, just more slowly.

chapters.title: Down the Stair Under the River
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Using a forged guild writ, she slips past the wardens and descends the old stair beneath the falls into the under-court, where everything bought and forgotten accumulates. Emotional beat: awe laced with terror; the deeper she goes, the more the place seems to already know her name.

chapters.title: The Queen of Kept Things
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The queen offers a courteous tour of her hoard — including shelves of souls shelved like ledgers — and reveals the price for the child's return: a soul of equal weight, due at the next new moon. Emotional beat: seduction and horror; the queen is kind the way a collector is kind to a specimen.

chapters.title: New Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Above ground, the Guildmaster discovers Mirabel's theft of the writ and sends Dominic to retrieve her before the bargain can unravel a century of guild contracts. Dominic instead burns his own writ of protection and follows her down. Emotional beat: love choosing sides at last, at real cost.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Soul
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Reunited, they attempt the exchange, but the queen's scale rejects every substitute — coin, memory, years — and the prophecy's last line becomes legible only now: the debt closes on Mirabel herself. Emotional beat: despair at the trap closing exactly as written, and the question of whether prophecy is fate or merely a first draft.

chapters.title: Amendment
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Mirabel offers not her soul but her authorship — she amends the contract in the Guild's own binding style, inserting a clause the century-old brokers never anticipated, while Dominic stakes his guild-standing as surety. Emotional beat: triumph through craft; the ledger-keeper beats the court at paperwork.

chapters.title: Everything Owed, Everything Kept
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The child wakes by the river; the queen keeps the promised payment — Mirabel's memories of Dominic — and the Guild, exposed, must reckon with what it brokered. Dominic leaves the Guild entirely and begins courting her memory back, one true story at a time. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — found family survives, truth wins, and love starts over from the first page.
